name: List Repeater (the only grid primitive)
description: Repeats a custom row template once per row of a dataset. This is THE grid primitive in this engine — there is no data-grid widget. Documented here as an atom (the repeater itself and its full prop set) separately from molecules/grid-row-template.json, which documents the row template that goes inside it.
sourceRefs: examples/fapo-fapi-full-breakdown.md 3.4 (DsFrmDetails1, full prop set), PART 5.1 (DsFrmDetails2, minimal prop set)

datasets.description: Array of dataset names to iterate. Only ever one entry in observed usage, e.g. ["DsFrmDetails1"].

watch.description: Datasets whose changes force a re-render. Include the HEADER dataset here, not just the row dataset, whenever a header value affects row display (e.g. VAT treatment). Omitting it is why rows go stale after header edits.

className.description: "TableListSect" always; add " facts-input-list" (space-separated) when rows contain editable inputs.

content.template.description: Always "custom" — no other value observed anywhere in the codebase.

content.props.description: Props applied to each rendered row wrapper. Set resolvestyles:true here to enable a per-row dynamic background.

editableRows.description: Full prop set, for grids whose rows contain inputs and whose appearance depends on header state or per-row status.

readOnlyRows.description: Minimal prop set, for display-only grids (no watch/filter props observed on these).

rowBackgroundNote: Two mutually exclusive conventions exist for row-level status colouring. (a) inline style: content.props.style.backgroundColor = "[this.bgColor]" with resolvestyles:true — driven by a bgColor field on the row. (b) className: row sect className = "[raw.facts-row-[this.row_error]]" with resolveprops:true — driven by a row_error field. Pick one per grid; do not mix them in the same row template.
scrollContainerNote: The list is normally wrapped in a sect that owns the scrollbar: {"item":true,"xs":12,"style":{"minHeight":"6vh","maxHeight":"50vh","overflow":"scroll"}}. Put the scroll on this wrapper, never on the page root.
